summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload under it
details: @servicetitan/json-render-react@0.4.10 declares a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into a temporary directory, chmods the extracted `bun` binary executable, and invokes it (`execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])`) against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) obfuscated in obfuscator.io style — shuffled string array with a self-mutating de-shuffler and hex-mangled identifiers — and is not referenced by the package's own `dist/index.js`, which advertises a JSON UI renderer. The published README documents a React JSON-schema rendering library and does not mention Bun, native runtimes, or an install-time payload. Fetching a second language runtime solely to execute an opaque, obfuscated local bundle at install time — where the payload deliberately targets a runtime most scanners and reviewers will not evaluate — is an install-time-RCE / alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; the payload's capabilities (network egress, filesystem access, credential reads) cannot be audited without full deobfuscation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
